summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with redness, swelling, and pain in his right second toe, which had been chronically discolored and previously lost its nail. He was at high risk for infection due to recent autologous stem cell transplant. Initial treatment included IV vancomycin for suspected MRSA. Imaging revealed bony destruction concerning for osteomyelitis. After lack of improvement, podiatry performed an incision and drainage, followed by a more extensive debridement. Foot culture grew coagulase-negative staphylococcus, sensitive to vancomycin. Vascular studies showed adequate perfusion despite moderate peripheral vascular disease. Anticoagulation was transitioned from heparin back to warfarin. The patient improved clinically, was transitioned to oral minocycline, and discharged home with crutches, non-weight-bearing on the right foot, and instructions to continue outpatient medications including aspirin for secondary prevention.
